title: "code-style"
subtitle: "Named visual treatments for code blocks in Quarto"
format:
  html:

filters:
  - code-style
---

A Quarto extension that decorates code blocks with **named styles** —
diff, emphasis, custom — applied to **regions** (lines, columns, regex
tokens) across **steps** (revealjs fragments).

Diff is one preset. The engine doesn't know what a diff is.

## Install

```bash
quarto add EmilHvitfeldt/quarto-code-diff
```

Then in your document's YAML:

```yaml
filters:
  - code-style
```

## Quick taste

```{.r data-code-style="add:2-3, rem:5"}
df |>
  filter(cyl == 6) |>
  group_by(gear) |>
  summarise(m = mean(mpg)) |>
  arrange(desc(m))
```

## Authoring forms

### Compact attribute (any code block)

```
{.r data-code-style="add:2-3, rem:5"}                # static
{.r data-code-style="|hi:2|rem:3,add:4-7|hi:8"}      # progressive
```

### YAML cell option (executable chunks)

```yaml
#| code-style:
#|   preset: emphasis
#|   styles:
#|     warn: { bg: "#fff3bf", gutter: "#f08c00", marker: "!" }
#|   transition: { duration: 400, mode: slide }
#|   steps:
#|     - focus: 3
#|     - warn: { line: 4, match: "bug", label: "this one" }
```

## Concepts

- **Style** — name → CSS class (preset) or inline primitives
  (`bg`, `fg`, `gutter`, `opacity`, `weight`, `marker`, `duration`, `easing`).
- **Region** — `at: 2-3`, `at: { line, match }`, `at: { line, cols }`,
  or short keys: `add: 2-3`.
- **Step** — top-level list = reveal.js fragments. Single object = static.

## Accessibility

- Transitions wrap `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)`.
- Every style ships a gutter `marker` character so colorblind / monochrome
  viewers can still read the decoration.
- Step labels are announced via an `aria-live` region.

## Debugging

Append `?cs-debug=1` to any rendered URL to surface inline error banners
above blocks with malformed specs, unknown style names, or out-of-range
line numbers.
